messages:
ana: FYI ran an nsys capture during a tail-latency incident on prod-rt. Seeing repeated host->device allocations aligned with 99th pct spikes. nsys trace: https://perf.rw/trace/abc123

bjorn: can you paste the kernel timeline screenshot? that pattern often means allocator churn not kernel slowness

ana: perfetto link: https://perfetto.rw/trace/def456  — timeline shows a series of ~2–3ms cudaMalloc spikes at batch boundaries, then tiny kernels. KV cache miss rate also jumps at the same points.

cheng: what nsys command did you run so I can reproduce locally?

ana: used this quick capture:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=alloc-sample --capture-range=cpu:start-capture-end --sample=none
```
(note: we used --trace=nvtx to preserve our app spans)

maria: my 2c: batching heuristics probably widened the merge window which increases concurrent small allocations. we've seen similar fragmentation with small-alloc-heavy traffic.

bjorn: also check the pool slab sizing. if slabs are smaller than working set we get cross-slab fragmentation + free-list contention.

ana: current node pool config (from /etc/redwood/env): REDWOOD_POOL_SLAB=8MB, REDWOOD_ARENA_CHUNK=16MB, REDWOOD_POOL_MAX_POOLS=2

ops-bot: node metadata: instance=g5.x2, driver=535.54, cuda=12.2, kernel=6.1

cheng: try increasing REDWOOD_POOL_SLAB -> 32MB and enable coalescing for a canary. also reduce batch merge window from 8ms -> 4ms to limit simultaneous tiny alloc bursts.

maria: +1. Also consider making KV cache more aggressive on prefix hits to reduce transient misses that cause allocations.

bjorn: there is also a fallback kernel path (fp16->int8 conversion path) triggered for short sequences; that path allocates temporary buffers. pin to the fp16 fastpath for the canary.

ana: I ran a 2hr canary with: slab=32MB, coalesce=true, merge_window=4ms, forced fp16 path. Tail dropped from ~210ms -> ~95ms. Still saw rare 3ms malloc spikes but far less frequent.

ana: attached flamegraph excerpt: https://perf.rw/fg/ghi789 (highlights allocator hotspots between kernel handoffs).

cheng: nice. We should also tune the defrag threshold — current defrag runs only when free_pct < 20% which might be too late.

maria: proposal: trigger defrag at free_pct < 35% and add a background async consolidation every 60s to coalesce small frees before they fragment.

bjorn: alternative if fragmentation persists: move to multi-bucket slab allocator (powers-of-two buckets) or buddy allocator. Slab bumping is cheaper short-term.

ana: quick config I deployed to canary:
```
REDWOOD_POOL_SLAB=33554432
REDWOOD_ARENA_CHUNK=67108864
REDWOOD_POOL_COALESCE=1
REDWOOD_BATCH_MERGE_MS=4
REDWOOD_DEFRAG_TRIGGER_PCT=35
REDWOOD_DEFRAG_INTERVAL_S=60
RDW_MODEL_FORCE_FP16=1
```

dev-bot: rolling canary -> 5 nodes in eng-runtime cluster (started at 2026-03-18T02:10:00Z)

maria: dashboards updated (per-route): per-token allocs, kvcache-miss-rate, pool-fragmentation-pct, per-node-tail-latency. Alerts: kvcache-miss-rate > 5% now fires to eng-runtime on-call.

ana: next steps: 1) schedule full-night nsys captures across more node types 2) run defrag threshold sweep under synthetic traffic 3) add allocator histogram sampling to get allocation size distribution heatmaps 4) revisit kernel-selection rules for small vs long sequences.

bjorn: if we still see fragmentation after 32MB slabs we'll prototype multi-bucket slabs. also check for any host-thread preemption that may exacerbate allocation stalls.

cheng: I'll open a tracking ticket with links to traces and the canary results.

ana: created RW-5412: includes perfetto/nsys links, canary config, flamegraph, and observed SLA improvements. assigned to eng-runtime.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks everyone, great iteration.
